disease_label_per_paper: Life-threatening severe babesiosis with overwhelming parasitemia in an asplenic patient
presentation_summary: 68-year-old man with traumatic asplenia and hypertension was admitted for fever and altered mental status after six days of fever, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.
He lived in a wooded New England area, enjoyed hiking, denied recent travel or transfusion, and had recently completed a prednisone taper for Bell's palsy.

Outside-hospital labs showed WBC 21.9 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 11.5 g/dL, platelet count 31 x10^9/L, total bilirubin 9.6 mg/dL, creatinine 4.68 mg/dL, BUN 98 mg/dL, lactate 7.1 mmol/L, and Babesia parasitemia 64.2%.

On transfer, labs showed hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, platelets 32 x10^9/L, creatinine 4.43 mg/dL, total bilirubin 10.5 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 5.0 mg/dL, AST 316 U/L, LDH 3072 U/L, haptoglobin <10 mg/dL, and Babesia parasitemia 51.6%.
He underwent two red-cell exchange sessions plus antiparasitic therapy; parasitemia fell to 9.8% after the first exchange, 1.8% after the second, <0.1% by day 7, and smear-negative by day 14.
